chunks: Al-Shaykh — may Allah the Exalted support him — from Abu al-Qasim Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Qulawayh, from Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Mu'ammar ibn Khallad — he said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man who has an ailment and cannot lie down, for whom wudu is difficult, and who sits leaning against pillows; sometimes he dozes off while sitting in that condition. He said: «He must perform wudu.» I said: Wudu is indeed difficult for him. He said: «When sound becomes hidden from him (inaudible), then wudu has become obligatory upon him.»

End of the hadith. His statement (peace be upon him) — «When sound becomes hidden from him, wudu has become obligatory upon him» — indicates what [the scholar] mentioned regarding renewal of wudu due to: fainting (igmā'), bilious fits (marra), and everything that prevents dhikr (conscious awareness). He then mentioned after that: urine, wind, excrement, and janaba.

What indicates that is: what al-Shaykh — may Allah support him — informed me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from his father, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurara — he said:

I said to Abu Ja'far and Abu 'Abd Allah (peace be upon them both): What nullifies wudu? They both said: «What exits from your two lower orifices — the penis and the anus — of excrement, urine, semen, or wind; and sleep until it removes the intellect. All sleep is disliked (makruh) unless you are still hearing sound.»

This hadith has been mentioned previously. As for what he mentioned after that — menstruation (hayd), irregular vaginal bleeding (istihada), postpartum bleeding (nifas), and touching the dead — these are things that necessitate ghusl. When they necessitate ghusl, they also necessitate ritual purity (tahara), because the minor ritual purity (al-tahara al-sughra) is subsumed within the major (al-kubra). When the major is invalidated, it is logically impossible for the minor to subsist after it. I will mention hereafter what indicates that these require ghusl in their respective chapters, God willing. As for his statement: «Nothing from among the ritual nullifiers (ahdath) necessitates tahara under any circumstance other than what we have mentioned» — the proof for that is what he informed me.

key_terms.اَلْأَحْدَاثُ: ritual nullifiers (acts or states that invalidate wudu or ghusl)
key_terms.اَلْإِغْمَاءُ: fainting; loss of consciousness (a wudu nullifier)

ai.seo_question: What are the nullifiers of wudu according to Imams al-Ridha, al-Baqir and al-Sadiq (AS) in Tahdhib al-Ahkam?
ai.summary: This composite entry from Tahdhib al-Ahkam presents two hadiths and jurisprudential commentary by al-Tusi on the nullifiers of wudu (al-ahdath). Imam al-Ridha (AS) rules that a sick person sitting leaning on pillows who dozes off must renew wudu when sound becomes inaudible to him — establishing auditory consciousness as the criterion of wakefulness. Imams al-Baqir and al-Sadiq (AS) then enumerate all nullifiers comprehensively; al-Tusi adds that hayd, nifas, istihada, and touching the dead require ghusl, which by logical subsumption also invalidates the minor purity.
